correctness.rationale: For a<0 the primitive nonnegative companion matrix has a unique Perron root, and its scalar equation gives the exact lower Schur boundary. For 0<a<a_plus an exact multiplied-polynomial identity and a strict reverse-triangle inequality exclude every unit-circle root; root continuity then yields Schur stability. At a_plus only -1 lies on the unit circle, its derivative is strictly negative, and beyond a_plus there is a real root less than -1. The model equilibrium coefficient transform is an exact monotone rational function of total population. A bundled checker passes 371 supporting exact and numerical assertions. All signs, dimensions and equality boundaries were reconstructed independently in the proof; finite checks are not used to infer generality.

originality.rationale: The 2023 preprint and its 2024 revision derive a candidate odd-age flip threshold but explicitly leave the general p>1/2 interval as a conjecture supported numerically. Wikan (2012) numerically asserted the same qualitative first-flip pattern, and Wikan--Kristensen (2017) repeated that qualitative pattern without presenting an all-odd-degree proof; thus neither the observation nor the candidate boundary is claimed as new. The new assertion is an exact full-real-coefficient necessary-and-sufficient Schur interval, its proof for all odd degrees and all p in (0,1), strict absence of intervening complex crossings, simple outward crossing, and the sharp gamma-dependent feasibility criterion for finite-population instability. Searches did not reveal the complete proof, but all-parameter general polynomial stability theory could conceivably subsume it.
residual_risks: Old 2012 and 2017 papers asserted the qualitative first-flip pattern, so there is no novelty claim for the phenomenon or predicted boundary.
An unlocated abstract Schur-stability theorem for a trinomial or geometric companion family may entail the result despite lack of a matched source.
An independent audit of the proof and literature priority has not been performed.

value.rationale: The explicit first-loss problem at arbitrary odd numbers of age classes and high survival p>1/2 was raised as a specific conjecture in the 2023 preprint and 2024 paper. This result replaces its numerical examples and sufficient criterion with a complete all-degree exact Schur classification, proving no complex pair crosses first. The derived gamma cutoff distinguishes models with and without any finite-population linear instability. The motivation and exact invariant arise directly from a widely used age-structured nonlinear recruitment model, not an arbitrary finite numerical slice.
